html:
The Battle of San Pasqual was fought on 6 and 7 December 1846 in the San Pasqual Valley, near today's San Diego, California, United States. About 150 American soldiers under General Stephen Kearny fought about 75 Californio lancers under Andrés Pico. Both sides claimed the victory, but the Americans lost far more men.

It was part of the Mexican-American War. Kearny had taken New Mexico without a fight and set out for California, then a province of Mexico. On the way he heard it was already in American hands and sent most of his men back. In fact the Californios, the Spanish-speaking settlers, had risen and retaken Los Angeles. Kearny's men arrived worn out from the desert, on tired mules and with damp gunpowder. At dawn they charged in a strung-out line. The lancers turned and cut them up, killing about 20 and wounding Kearny. The Americans held a hill for four days, eating their mules, until sailors and marines from San Diego reached them.

Kearny then joined the navy's forces and retook Los Angeles in January 1847, ending the fighting in California. In 1848 Mexico gave up California to the United States, just as the Gold Rush began.
